title: Soybeans: protein, fat, and nutritional value

seo.title: Soybeans: protein, fat, fiber, and calories
seo.meta_description: Cooked mature soybeans provide about 18 g protein, 9 g fat, 6 g fiber, and 172 calories per 100 g. Dry beans look much more concentrated because they contain less water.
seo.search_intent: Understand soybean nutrition and why values differ between dry and cooked soybeans.

excerpt: Cooked mature soybeans are among the highest-protein legumes, with about 18 g protein, 9 g fat, 6 g fiber, and 172 calories per 100 g. Dry soybeans exceed 35 g protein per 100 g, but that number is not directly comparable because cooking adds water and increases weight.
content_html:
Soy is a legume, but nutritionally it does not look exactly like lentils, chickpeas, or beans. It provides more protein and considerably more fat, which helps explain both its higher energy density and the wide range of foods made from it.

Cooked soybeans are the more useful reference

Comparing 100 g of dry soybeans with 100 g of cooked legumes creates an artificial gap. Soybeans absorb water during cooking, gain weight, and become less concentrated per 100 g.

NutrientCooked mature soybeans, 100 g1 cup-ish serving, 180 g
Calories~172~310
Protein~18.2 g~32.8 g
Fat~9.0 g~16.2 g
Fiber~6.0 g~10.8 g
Carbohydrate~8.4 g~15.1 g

A generous serving can therefore provide more than 30 g of protein, which is unusually high for a cooked legume.

Why dry soybeans look twice as high in protein

Dry soybeans are around 36 g protein per 100 g. Once cooked, absorbed water increases the total weight, spreading the same protein across a larger mass.

Cooking has not destroyed half the protein. The main explanation is water dilution.

Fat is a major difference from other legumes

Cooked lentils and many beans contain less than 1 g fat per 100 g. Cooked soybeans are closer to 9 g. That helps explain why soybeans provide around 172 calories per 100 g while many other cooked legumes are lower.

Much of soy fat is unsaturated, with a substantial polyunsaturated component. Soybeans also provide ALA, a plant omega-3.

High-quality protein for a plant food

Soy contains all nine essential amino acids and has relatively high protein quality compared with many plant foods. That does not mean other legumes are nutritionally useless or that every meal must contain soy.

It does mean tofu, tempeh, cooked soybeans, and soy milk can be especially useful protein foods in vegetarian and vegan diets.

Fiber, iron, and other micronutrients

Whole soybeans retain fiber that is much lower in some refined soy products. They also provide iron, magnesium, potassium, phosphorus, and folate, although phytates can reduce absorption of some minerals.

Soybeans, edamame, tofu, and soy milk are not interchangeable

Edamame is immature soybean and contains more water. Tofu is made from coagulated soy milk and varies widely by firmness and coagulant. Tempeh retains the whole fermented bean and is more concentrated. Soy milk is much more diluted.

So “soy” cannot be represented by one nutrient number across every soy food.

The useful takeaway

Cooked mature soybeans combine something unusual among legumes: high protein, fiber, and a meaningful amount of unsaturated fat. Always compare foods in the same state instead of matching dry soybeans against cooked lentils or beans.

faq.question: How much protein is in cooked soybeans?
faq.answer: Cooked mature soybeans provide about 18 g protein per 100 g; a 180 g serving can provide roughly 33 g.

faq.question: Why do dry soybeans have more protein per 100 g?
faq.answer: They contain much less water. Cooking adds water and spreads the protein across a greater weight.

faq.question: Are soybeans high in fat?
faq.answer: They contain more fat than most legumes, about 9 g per 100 g cooked, with most of the fat unsaturated.
